app.tagline: Is it safe to breathe today?
app.subtitle: Free · No sign-up · Open data
app.headline: Is it safe to breathe today?
app.lede: Air-quality numbers are everywhere. Clear answers aren't. AirAware tells you what today's air means for you — and what to do about it.
app.placeholder_body: Enter a location and choose who it's for. We'll read the live air and tell you what to do.
app.error_generic: Couldn't reach the air-quality service. Check your connection and try again.
app.error_location_denied: Location permission denied — type a place instead.
app.error_location_unavailable: Couldn't get your location — type a place instead.
app.error_geolocation_unsupported: Geolocation isn't supported on this device.
app.why_this_advice: Advice follows US EPA AQI category guidance.
app.why_sensitive: Risk is raised one band because sensitive groups should act sooner (US EPA guidance).
app.data_source_body: live air quality & geocoding from Open-Meteo — free, open, no tracking
app.index_regional: US EPA AQI (primary) + {system} for your country
app.foot_disclaimer: Informational, not a substitute for medical advice.
app.cig_meaning_body: Based on the Berkeley Earth equivalence: breathing about 22 µg/m³ of PM2.5 for a day carries roughly the harm of one cigarette. It's a long-term comparison to make an invisible number feel real — not a medical figure.
app.cig_week: ≈ {total} cigarettes over the last {days} days you checked (on this device).
app.indoor_intro: Keep the windows closed and filter your indoor air.
app.indoor_1: Run a HEPA purifier sized to the room (CADR near the room's area in ft²).
app.indoor_2: No purifier? A box fan with a taped-on MERV-13 filter (a Corsi-Rosenthal box) works well.
app.indoor_3: Pick one room to keep cleanest — close its door and run the filter there.
app.indoor_4: Ventilate only when outdoor air is better than indoor; otherwise keep it sealed.

pollutant_causes.smoke: Fine particles (PM2.5) dominate — typically smoke from wildfires, burning, or combustion.
pollutant_causes.dust: Coarse particles (PM10) dominate — often wind-blown dust or sand.
pollutant_causes.ozone_smog: Ground-level ozone (smog), which builds up in hot, sunny, stagnant air.
pollutant_causes.traffic: Nitrogen dioxide, mostly from traffic and combustion.
pollutant_causes.industrial: Sulfur dioxide, usually from industry or burning fossil fuels.
pollutant_causes.combustion: Carbon monoxide from combustion — traffic, heating, or fire.
pollutant_causes.mixed: A mix of everyday urban sources.

app.no_saved: No saved places yet. Save a place to get alerts when air quality changes.
app.alert_permission_denied: Notifications blocked. Enable them in your browser settings to get alerts.
app.alert_permission_granted: You'll be notified when air quality rises above your threshold.

who.title: Built for the people air hits hardest
who.sub: Smoke and smog aren't equal-opportunity. These groups get protective advice sooner.
who.respiratory_body: Fine-particle smoke can trigger attacks well before the air looks "bad".
who.heart_body: Pollution stresses the cardiovascular system, raising real risk.
who.child_body: Smaller, developing lungs take in more air per kilo of body weight.
who.pregnant_body: Exposure is linked to outcomes for both parent and baby.
who.older_body: Reduced lung reserve makes poor air more dangerous.
who.outdoor_body: Hours of exertion outside multiply every exposure.

how.title: From a place name to a plan
how.footer_copy: A public-good project. Free to use, open data, no tracking. Air quality and geocoding from Open-Meteo; guidance follows US EPA AQI categories.
